[UI] Update Font Size — Flutter Migration

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter. Source reference: In the RN app, fonts are loaded at bootstrap (OpenSans-Regular, OpenSans-Bold via expo-font in src/pages/init.js) and font sizes are scattered inline across *.style.js files. The migration should consolidate this into a single Flutter typography scale.

Goal

Establish a centralized, consistent typography / font-size system in the Flutter app and apply it across screens, replacing the ad-hoc per-component font sizes from the RN codebase.

Scope

  • Register the OpenSans family (Regular + Bold) in pubspec.yaml and ThemeData.textTheme.
  • Define a typographic scale (e.g. display / title / body / caption) as reusable TextStyles rather than hardcoded sizes.
  • Audit current RN font sizes and map them to the new scale.
  • Ensure text scales correctly with device text-size / accessibility settings.

Out of Scope

  • Full screen-by-screen UI rebuild (tracked separately, see [Main] Update UI).
  • Localization content (handled by i18n migration).

Acceptance Criteria

  • OpenSans Regular + Bold registered and rendering in the Flutter app.
  • A single source of truth for font sizes (theme text styles), no hardcoded magic numbers in widgets.
  • Typography scale documented (name → size/weight) for the team.
  • Text respects system font-scaling without breaking layout on small/large devices.
  • Visual parity with the RN app's key screens (titles, body, buttons, captions).

Grounded in docs/analyze.md §3 (stack/structure) and the consistency goals in §4.

Demo by Developer

[Main] Update UI — Flutter Migration

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter. Source reference: The RN Main / Home screen is the project-list / dashboard entry point (src/pages/main, src/pages/home — see docs/analyze.md §3.2). It is the first screen after Init (see Rooter) and lists the user's local tour projects with their upload/sync status.

Goal

Build the Main screen UI in Flutter to match (and modernize) the RN app's project dashboard, using the new typography system and component conventions.

Scope

  • Recreate the Main/Home layout: project list, per-project status (draft / uploaded / published), and primary actions (open, create new tour).
  • Use the centralized typography scale (see [UI] Update Font Size) and a reusable widget structure (cards/list items, navbar, sidebar).
  • Wire the list to the local DB layer (see [App] Setup Local DB) so projects render from local data.
  • Empty state + loading state for the project list.

Out of Scope

  • Project Detail / capture / connection editing screens (separate migration tasks).
  • Backend upload flow (separate task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Main screen renders the list of local tour projects from the local DB.
  • Each item shows name, address, and sync/upload status indicator.
  • Primary actions present: create new tour, open existing project.
  • Loading and empty states implemented.
  • Layout responsive across phone sizes; visual parity with the RN Main screen.
  • Uses shared typography + components (no one-off styles).

Grounded in docs/analyze.md §2 (capabilities), §3.2 (structure), and §6 (consistency recommendations).

Demo by Developer

[App] Setup Local DB — Flutter Migration

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter. Source reference: The RN app is offline-first and stores all tour data locally in SQLite (WAL mode), defined and migrated in src/pages/init.js. The Flutter app must replicate this local persistence layer. See docs/analyze.md §3.3 for the full data model.

Goal

Set up the local SQLite database in the Flutter app (e.g. sqflite / drift), recreating the existing schema and a clean migration mechanism, as the foundation for offline tour authoring.

Schema to replicate (from docs/analyze.md §3.3)

  • projects — id, project_name, address, user_id, project_type, uploaded, googleUploaded, isAutoConnect, virtual_tour_status, listing, attr, timestamps.
  • panoramas — id, panorama_original/thumbnail/small/tiny, latlng, heading, fov, width/height, level_id, project_id, uploaded, pano_id, stitching_id.
  • connections — id, main_id, link_id, meters, angle, draft, auto_connect_error, project_id.
  • levels — id, level_name, level_type, position, folder_id, project_id.

Scope

  • Initialize the DB on app start (equivalent of RN Init bootstrap) and create the 4 tables.
  • Implement a versioned migration system (improving on the RN PRAGMA table_info hand-rolled approach — see analysis §5/§6) so schema changes are tracked by version.
  • Provide a data-access layer (DAO/repository) with typed models for each table.
  • Enable WAL mode for concurrency parity.

Out of Scope

  • Cloud sync / upload to GoThru APIs (separate task).
  • Filesystem panorama image storage (separate task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • DB initializes on first launch; the 4 tables (projects, panoramas, connections, levels) are created.
  • Versioned migration runner in place (no ad-hoc column-existence checks).
  • Typed Dart models + DAO/repository for CRUD on each table.
  • Basic round-trip verified: insert → query → update → delete a project and related panoramas/connections.
  • WAL mode enabled; offline read/write works with no network.

Directly addresses docs/analyze.md §3.3 (data model) and the migration-robustness recommendations in §5/§6.

Implement the "Create Tour" flow for the Real Estate tour type in the Flutter app: the user starts a new tour, selects/branches into the Real Estate type, fills the required real-estate metadata, and a project is persisted locally with the correct project_type and listing data.

  • Persist a projects row with project_type = real estate, listing = 1, address, and attr populated.

  • Validation for required fields; localized labels.

Out of Scope

  • Upload/publish to GoThru (separate task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Real Estate option available in the Create Tour flow.
  • Required real-estate fields validated before a project is created.
  • New project saved locally with correct project_type, listing = 1, address, and attr.
  • On success, user lands in the new project ready to add content.
  • Labels sourced from i18n; works offline (local persistence only).

[Level] Integrate Default Level (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter. Source reference: RN multi-level support — the levels table groups panoramas into floors/levels, and panoramas default to level_id = 1 (see docs/analyze.md §2.4 and §3.3). When a tour is created it must have a usable default level so panoramas have somewhere to belong before the user adds more levels.

Goal

Ensure every newly created tour automatically gets a default level, and that panoramas added without an explicit level are assigned to it — replicating the RN behavior in the Flutter app on top of the new local DB layer.

Scope

  • On project creation, create a default levels row for the project (e.g. default name / position 0).
  • Assign new panoramas to the default level (level_id) when no level is chosen.
  • Default level appears in the level list/selector for the project.
  • Default level is not duplicated on subsequent opens of the same project.

  • Full level management UI (add/rename/reorder/delete levels) — separate task.
  • Moving panoramas between levels — separate task.

  • Creating a tour produces exactly one default level for that project.
  • Panoramas added without a chosen level are linked to the default level.
  • Default level is visible/selectable in the project.
  • Reopening the project does not create duplicate default levels.
  • Behavior works offline (local DB only) and survives app restart.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

  2. Expected: Confirmation/labels translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS Regression watch: discard reverts only the current listing's unsaved edits — no server data is changed.

issues.display_title: Issue #53: [Listing Detail] Virtual Tour Activate & Deactivate
issues.main_description_html:
[Listing Detail] Virtual Tour Activate & Deactivate (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter. Source reference: Projects carry virtual_tour_status (see docs/analyze.md §3.3); listing detail lets the user toggle a tour's live/active state via the GoThru API (§2.6/§3.4).

Goal

Implement Activate / Deactivate of a virtual tour in Listing Detail: toggle the tour's live status (virtual_tour_status) on GoThru, with clear current-state display.

Scope

  • A toggle/action to activate or deactivate the virtual tour.
  • Call the GoThru API to set status; update local virtual_tour_status and UI.
  • Confirmation for deactivation (since it affects public visibility); progress + result feedback.

Out of Scope

  • Publish Google / update tour / reload / discard (separate tasks).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Current active/inactive state is clearly shown.
  • Activate sets the tour live; Deactivate takes it offline (virtual_tour_status updated).
  • Deactivation asks for confirmation.
  • API errors surfaced with retry; state stays consistent after restart.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Activate (happy path)

  1. Open an inactive listing → Activate.
  2. Expected: Tour becomes active; status reflects active.

TC-2 — Deactivate with confirmation

  1. On an active listing → Deactivate → confirm.
  2. Expected: Tour becomes inactive; status reflects inactive.

TC-3 — Cancel deactivation

  1. Tap Deactivate, then cancel.
  2. Expected: Tour stays active; no change.

TC-4 — Offline / API error

  1. Toggle while offline or simulate error.
  2. Expected: Clear error; state not changed locally without server confirmation.

TC-5 — State persistence

  1. Toggle, relaunch, reopen.
  2. Expected: The new status persists/refetches correctly.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: State labels/confirmation translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS Regression watch: toggling status does not alter tour content (panoramas/connections).

[Listing Detail] Update Tour (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter. Source reference: RN listing detail (src/pages/listings-detail) manages a published/listed tour on GoThru; see docs/analyze.md §2.6 (listings), §2.7 (publish), §3.4 (listings API apil.gothru.co), and projects fields in §3.3.

Goal

Implement "Update Tour" in Listing Detail: push edits made to a listed tour (metadata and/or panorama changes) back to GoThru so the live listing reflects the latest state.

Scope

  • Update action that sends changed listing/tour data to the GoThru API.
  • Reflect server response in local state (status, updated timestamps).
  • Progress + success/failure feedback; respect connectivity.

Out of Scope

  • Publishing to Google (separate task); activate/deactivate (separate task); discarding changes (separate task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Update sends the current changes to GoThru and confirms success.
  • Local state reflects the updated server status after success.
  • Requires connectivity; clear error + retry on failure (no silent failure).
  • Works with the signed-in session token; labels via i18n.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Update a listed tour (happy path)

  1. Open a listing → make a change → Update Tour.
  2. Expected: Update succeeds; listing reflects the new data; success confirmation.

TC-2 — No changes

  1. Tap Update with nothing changed.
  2. Expected: Graceful no-op / informs nothing to update.

TC-3 — Offline

  1. Attempt update offline.
  2. Expected: Clear "no internet" message; update not started.

TC-4 — API error + retry

  1. Simulate a server error, then retry.
  2. Expected: Error surfaced; retry completes successfully.

TC-5 — Persistence

  1. Update, relaunch, reopen the listing.
  2. Expected: Updated state persists/refetches consistently.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: Labels/status/errors translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS Regression watch: other listings unaffected by an update to one.

[Listing Detail] Publish Google (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter. Source reference: RN publishes tours to Google (Street View / Business Profile); projects track googleUploaded (see docs/analyze.md §2.7 and §3.3). Uses the GoThru/Google integration.

Goal

Implement "Publish Google" in Listing Detail: publish the listed tour to Google, updating the publish state (googleUploaded) and surfacing the result.

Scope

  • Publish-to-Google action for the current listing/tour.
  • Trigger the GoThru-side Google publish flow; show progress and outcome.
  • Update local googleUploaded/publish status on success; handle Google auth/permission requirements.

Out of Scope

  • Update tour / activate-deactivate / reload / discard (separate tasks).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Publish-to-Google action triggers the publish flow and reports progress.
  • On success, the listing reflects a published-to-Google state (googleUploaded).
  • Auth/permission and API errors are surfaced clearly with retry.
  • Requires connectivity; works with the signed-in session.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Publish to Google (happy path)

  1. Open a listing eligible to publish → Publish Google.
  2. Expected: Publish completes; listing shows published-to-Google state.

TC-2 — Already published

  1. Publish a listing that is already on Google.
  2. Expected: Handled gracefully (informs already published / re-publish behavior defined).

TC-3 — Missing Google auth/permission

  1. Attempt publish without required Google authorization.
  2. Expected: Clear prompt/guidance; no crash.

TC-4 — Offline / API error

  1. Attempt publish offline or with a server error.
  2. Expected: Clear error; retry possible; state not corrupted.

TC-5 — Status persistence

  1. Publish, relaunch, reopen.
  2. Expected: Published-to-Google state persists/refetches.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: Labels/status/errors translated.

Platforms: Android + iOS Regression watch: GoThru listing state remains consistent with Google publish state.

[Tour Detail] Integrate Upload Tour (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter. Source reference: RN uploads finished tours to GoThru via /streeteditor/upload-tour (apil.gothru.co); see docs/analyze.md §2.7, §3.4, and the upload-reliability notes in §5.

Goal

Implement "Upload Tour" in the Flutter app: send a local tour (project + panoramas + connections + levels) to GoThru, with progress, pre-checks, and clear success/failure handling.

Scope

  • Pre-upload checks: connectivity, storage/quota, per-panorama GoThru existence (skip already-present panoramas).
  • Upload project metadata, panorama assets, connections, and levels.
  • Progress feedback (per-panorama / overall); update local uploaded / virtual_tour_status.
  • Surface errors with retry; no silent failure.

Out of Scope

  • Retry-condition fix specifics (tracked in the RN repo); moderation; Google publishing.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Upload sends the full tour and reflects true server state on completion (uploaded/virtual_tour_status).
  • Pre-checks (network, storage, per-panorama existence) run before/within upload.
  • Progress shown; already-uploaded panoramas are skipped (no duplicates).
  • Errors surfaced with retry; partial uploads are resumable/clean.
  • Works with the signed-in session token.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Upload a tour (happy path)

  1. Open a complete local tour → Upload.
  2. Expected: Upload completes; tour marked uploaded; appears correctly on GoThru.

TC-2 — Skip already-uploaded panoramas

  1. Upload a tour where some panoramas already exist on GoThru.
  2. Expected: Only missing panoramas are sent; no duplicates server-side.

TC-3 — Offline / no connection

  1. Attempt upload offline.
  2. Expected: Clear "no internet" message; upload not started.

TC-4 — Quota / storage exceeded

  1. Upload when over quota.
  2. Expected: Clear error; no broken partial state looping.

TC-5 — Interruption + retry

  1. Interrupt mid-upload, then retry.
  2. Expected: Resumes remaining work; completes; one tour, no duplicates.

TC-6 — Progress feedback

  1. Upload a large tour.
  2. Expected: Visible progress; UI not frozen.

Platforms: Android + iOS Regression watch: local tour data intact whether upload succeeds or fails.

[Tour Detail] Integrate Auto Level (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter. Source reference: RN multi-level support + project flag useAutoConnect/auto features and the levels model (docs/analyze.md §2.4, §3.3 levels, panoramas.level_id). Auto Level automatically organizes/assigns panoramas into levels rather than requiring fully manual grouping.

Goal

Implement "Auto Level" in Tour Detail: automatically assign the project's panoramas to levels (creating levels as needed), so multi-story/indoor tours are organized without fully manual level setup.

Scope

  • Trigger Auto Level for a project (action in Tour Detail / level management).
  • Run the auto-level logic (local and/or server-assisted) and assign each panorama a level_id, creating levels rows as needed.
  • Show progress and a summary of the result (levels created, panoramas assigned).
  • Result is editable afterward (does not lock manual level edits).

Out of Scope

  • Manual add/edit/delete level (separate tasks); Auto Label (separate task); auto-connect.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Auto Level assigns panoramas to levels and creates levels where needed.
  • Every panorama ends with a valid level_id (none orphaned).
  • Result summary shown; progress visible for large tours.
  • Auto-assigned levels remain manually editable afterward.
  • Works per the agreed online/offline behavior; errors surfaced (no silent failure).

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Run Auto Level (happy path)

  1. Open a tour with multiple panoramas → run Auto Level.
  2. Expected: Panoramas are grouped into levels; summary shows levels created/assignments.

TC-2 — All panoramas assigned

  1. After Auto Level, inspect panoramas.
  2. Expected: Each panorama has a valid level_id; none left unassigned/orphaned.

TC-3 — Editable after auto

  1. After Auto Level, manually rename/move a level/panorama.
  2. Expected: Manual edits work; auto result is not locked.

TC-4 — Re-run Auto Level

  1. Run Auto Level again on the same tour.
  2. Expected: Defined behavior (re-group or no duplicate levels); no corruption.

TC-5 — Single panorama / edge case

  1. Run on a tour with one panorama.
  2. Expected: Graceful result (assigned to a single/default level); no crash.

TC-6 — Error / connectivity (if server-assisted)

  1. Trigger with no connection (if it requires server).
  2. Expected: Clear handling/message; no half-applied state.

Platforms: Android + iOS Regression watch: existing levels/panorama images/connections not corrupted by auto-leveling.

[Tour Detail] Integrate Auto Label (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter. Source reference: RN project flag useAutoLabel (added to the projects table in src/pages/init.js); see docs/analyze.md §3.3. Auto Label automatically generates labels/names for panoramas (e.g. sequential or position-based) instead of manual naming.

Goal

Implement "Auto Label" in Tour Detail: automatically generate labels/names for the project's panoramas, controlled by the project's useAutoLabel setting, so users don't have to name each panorama manually.

Scope

  • Toggle/trigger Auto Label for a project (persist useAutoLabel).
  • Generate labels for panoramas (e.g. sequential / order- or position-based) and apply them.
  • Show the applied labels in the panorama list; result remains manually editable.
  • Re-apply consistently when panoramas are added (per the agreed rule).

Out of Scope

  • Auto Level (separate task); manual rename of individual panoramas (existing behavior).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Auto Label generates and applies labels to the project's panoramas.
  • The useAutoLabel setting persists on the project.
  • Labels are visible in the panorama list and remain manually editable.
  • Labeling is consistent/ordered; no duplicate/empty labels.
  • Works offline (local operation); survives restart.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Enable Auto Label (happy path)

  1. Open a tour → enable/run Auto Label.
  2. Expected: Panoramas receive generated labels; useAutoLabel is on.

TC-2 — Labels shown in list

  1. View the panorama list after labeling.
  2. Expected: Each panorama shows its auto-generated label.

TC-3 — Ordering/consistency

  1. Inspect labels across the tour.
  2. Expected: Labels follow the defined order rule; no duplicates/empties.

TC-4 — Manual override

  1. Manually rename an auto-labeled panorama.
  2. Expected: Manual label is kept (per the agreed override rule).

TC-5 — Add panorama after auto-label

  1. With Auto Label on, add a new panorama.
  2. Expected: It receives a label consistent with the scheme.

TC-6 — Persistence after restart

  1. Auto-label, relaunch, reopen.
  2. Expected: Labels and useAutoLabel setting persist.

Platforms: Android + iOS Regression watch: auto-labeling changes only labels — not images, levels, or connections.

issues.display_title: Issue #25: [Tour Detail] Update UX Capture Camera 360
issues.main_description_html:
[Tour Detail] Update UX Capture Camera 360 (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter. Source reference: RN camera capture flow (src/pages/camera-360, src/services/insta360.service.js) connects to an Insta360 over WiFi (OSC) and captures 360° images. See docs/analyze.md §2.1, §3.5, and the reliability/feedback recommendations in §5/§6.

Goal

Improve the UX of the Camera 360 capture flow in Tour Detail: make connection, capture, and import states clear and resilient, replacing ambiguous/silent states with explicit user feedback.

Scope

  • Clear connection status (searching / connected / disconnected) for the Insta360 camera.
  • Capture states: ready → capturing → downloading → imported, each with visible feedback.
  • Surfaced, actionable errors (camera not connected, capture failed, download failed) with retry.
  • Disable/guard the capture action while busy; prevent duplicate triggers.
  • Smooth return to the panorama list with the new capture highlighted.

Out of Scope

  • The underlying capture/import persistence (covered by the Add Panorama from Camera 360 task).
  • Insta360 SDK installation.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Connection status is always visible and accurate.
  • Each capture phase shows clear progress feedback (no silent waits).
  • Errors are surfaced with a retry path; no dead-end spinners.
  • Capture button is guarded while busy (no double-capture).
  • After capture, user returns to the list with the new panorama visible.
  • Labels via i18n.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Capture flow feedback (happy path)

  1. Connect camera → capture.
  2. Expected: UI shows connected → capturing → downloading → imported, each visibly; new panorama appears.

TC-2 — Camera not connected

  1. Open capture without the camera connected.
  2. Expected: Clear status + guidance; capture disabled until connected.

TC-3 — Connection lost mid-capture

  1. Disconnect camera WiFi during capture.
  2. Expected: Error surfaced with retry; no stuck spinner, no broken entry.

TC-4 — Double-trigger guard

  1. Rapidly tap capture multiple times.
  2. Expected: Only one capture runs; button disabled while busy.

TC-5 — Retry after failure

  1. Force a capture/download failure, then retry.
  2. Expected: Retry works and completes cleanly.

TC-6 — Localization

  1. Switch language during the flow.
  2. Expected: Status/error labels translated; no raw keys.

Platforms: Android (+ iOS where supported). Requires a physical Insta360 camera. Regression watch: add-from-phone flow and panorama list unaffected.
